title: Search Insert Position
statement: Given a sorted array nums and target, return the index where target exists or should be inserted.
think: What is the task asking? Given a sorted array nums and target, return the index where target exists or should be inserted.
What is the key operation? Identify the repeated action over the input.
What wording signals stand out? Same binary-search phrasing in Spot wording signals, plus where to insert in sorted order and boundary / index to return.
What is the brute force idea? Use extra loops or repeated checks.
What is the better/optimal idea? Use a clean binary search solution.
What are the edge cases? Empty-like input, single values, duplicates, and boundaries.
What is the complexity? For most of these easy tasks, aim for O(n) time unless sorting is required.
How would I explain it in an interview? State the pattern, the key operation, and the complexity.
algorithm: If not found, return left as insertion point
interview: I would solve it using Binary Search. I would first identify the core operation, then apply a simple binary search approach and mention the complexity.

whyThisPattern: This is a Binary Search on a boundary: the insert index is the first position that keeps the array sorted. Spot wording signals list general binary-search phrasing plus insert position and boundary.
whyNotOtherPatterns: Not Linear Scan, because sorted input allows a faster logarithmic search.
Not HashSet, because ordered boundaries matter.
